metaDescription: Five 12 to 18 inch cordless chainsaws at or under $200 compared on chain speed, battery setup, tensioning and safety, for storm cleanup and light firewood.
expertTake: The Snoonwee 42V is the best pick under this cap for a buyer who wants real limbing power, because it has a long bar, two batteries and a two-battery series design in one kit. The Greenworks 40V 12 inch is the value pick for a household that wants a named brand, auto-tensioning and a dual-action safety start. Anyone cutting seasoned hardwood daily should skip the category and step up to a premium platform saw.
introParagraphs: This is the price tier where a cordless chainsaw stops being a pruning toy and starts being a real tool. Bars grow from a few inches to a foot or more, and the saw can limb a fallen tree, cut up a storm-damaged branch pile or process a few loads of firewood.

The questions change at this size. Battery voltage and capacity, chain speed, tensioning method and safety features decide how the saw behaves under load, and the differences between a branded unit and an unbranded one show up in support rather than in the first cut.

products.name: Snoonwee 42V Max chainsaw, 16 and 18 inch bars, 2100W
products.description:
The Snoonwee is the only kit in this guide with two bar lengths, a 16 inch for nimble limbing and an 18 inch for bigger cuts. It runs two 4.0Ah packs in series to deliver a constant 42V maximum voltage, which helps the torque hold steady as the batteries drain. A brushless motor, rated at 2100 watts, handles the load.

The series design matters. Two packs in series raise voltage, and higher voltage gives more torque before the motor bogs down. The rating is a marketing figure, but a full-size bar and a two-battery layout are real hardware, and they put this saw closer to a branded full-size model than the 12 inch units below. Two chains are included, so a dull chain can be swapped and sharpened later.

The tradeoff is weight and unbranded support. A saw with an 18 inch bar and two packs is heavy over long sessions, and replacement packs come from the seller. Keep the oil reservoir full, check tension often, and wear eye protection and gloves.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want full-size bar lengths, two batteries and a spare chain for limbing and storm cleanup.
pros: 16 and 18 inch bars in one kit
Two packs in series hold voltage under load
cons: Rated wattage is not a measured figure

products.name: ReliaRoads 16 inch brushless chainsaw for DeWalt 20V MAX
products.description:
The ReliaRoads saw turns two DeWalt 20V MAX batteries you already own into a 40V cutting tool. It runs both packs at once, so it needs two batteries, and the listing does not include them. For a DeWalt owner with a spare pair, that is a very cheap way to get a 16 inch saw.

The chain speed claim of 54 feet per second is the number to notice. A fast chain cuts cleanly, and mini saws are around 28 feet per second, so this is a clear step up. Tool-free tensioning and automatic oiling remove two chores that otherwise require a wrench and attention.

Compared with the Snoonwee, it is cheaper if you own the batteries and more expensive if you do not, and it has a single bar length. It is a third-party tool that uses DeWalt packs, so warranty comes from the seller rather than DeWalt. Keep the packs charged and store the saw clean.
products.bestFor: Owners with a pair of DeWalt 20V MAX batteries who want a fast 16 inch saw.

products.name: Greenworks 40V 12 inch cordless chainsaw, 2.0Ah
products.description:
The Greenworks 40V is the most conventional saw in the group. It has a 12 inch bar, a 2.0Ah battery and charger in the kit, and a tool-free auto-tensioning system. A dual safety start, which needs both a lock and a trigger, helps prevent accidents.

The seller quotes about 50 cuts through 4 by 4 treated lumber on a single charge, which is a plausible small-job figure for a 2.0Ah pack. At 6 pounds it is light enough for most adults, and the low-recoil chain reduces kickback energy. It is a pruning and storm-cleanup saw, not a firewood machine.

Compared with the FXAFXA 12 inch, you give up bigger packs but gain a recognized brand and a battery that fits other Greenworks 40V tools. Keep the bar oiled, sharpen the chain and store the pack in a cool place.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want a mainstream brand, safe starting and a shared 40V battery.
pros: Brand makes replacement parts easier to find
cons: Less power than the series-battery saws

products.name: SEESII 12 inch brushless chainsaw, 1200W, 2 x 4.0Ah
products.description:
The Seesii 12 inch pairs a brushless motor with two 4.0Ah batteries and automatic oiling. Tool-free tensioning is part of the package, which saves a wrench in the field. For a household that wants one saw for pruning and light cutting, this is a well-rounded kit.

The 1200 watt number is a rating, not a measured output, and the saw is best judged by bar length, motor type and battery size. Two 4.0Ah packs give you a spare while one charges, which doubles your working time.

Compared with the Greenworks, it has bigger and more numerous batteries and a brushless motor but a less known brand. Against the Snoonwee, it has a shorter bar and lower voltage. Keep the reservoir filled and the chain sharp.
products.bestFor: Homeowners who want a 12 inch brushless saw with a spare battery.
cons: Rated wattage is a marketing figure

products.name: FXAFXA 12 inch 20V brushless chainsaw, 2 x 4.0Ah
products.description:
The FXAFXA is a 20V class saw with a brushless motor that spins at 12,000 RPM. It quotes a chain speed of up to 10 meters per second, which is about 33 feet per second, a step above the mini saws but below the faster full-size units. Two 4000 mAh batteries come in the kit.

A safety hand guard protects against flying debris, and overload protection guards the motor. The marketing lists a 2.56 horsepower figure, which is a rating and should not be compared with gas saw horsepower. Compared with the Seesii 12 inch, it has a lower chain speed claim and a lower-voltage platform.

It is a budget option for limbing and cleanup. Keep the chain oiled and sharp, and do not push the saw through hardwood quickly.
products.bestFor: Budget-minded buyers who want brushless power and two batteries.
pros: Lower cost than the larger kits
cons: Slower chain than the full-size saws
Horsepower claim is a marketing figure
20V platform lacks torque for big cuts

products.name: DOOYUTOOL 10 inch brushless chainsaw for DEWALT 20V MAX
products.description:
The DOOYUTOOL is the compact step between a mini pruning saw and the 12 inch group. Its 10 inch bar is long enough to take down a fallen branch, and a brushless motor keeps battery use reasonable. The kit includes a 4.0Ah pack, so it works out of the box, and it also accepts other DeWalt 20V MAX packs.

A self-oiling system with a see-through tank shows the reservoir level at a glance, which prevents the most common cause of chain damage. Its single-pack, 20V layout puts it well below the Snoonwee and ReliaRoads in torque, so it is a light limbing tool rather than a firewood saw. It is a third-party product that borrows DeWalt batteries, so support comes from the seller.

Compared with the Greenworks 12 inch, it has a shorter bar but a bigger battery in the box. Use it for trimming and storm cleanup, keep the chain sharp and store the pack indoors.
products.bestFor: Light limbing and cleanup, especially for owners of DeWalt 20V MAX batteries.
pros: See-through oil tank shows the level
Compact 10 inch bar is easy to control

buyingCriteria.explanation: A 16 or 18 inch bar, as on the Snoonwee, only helps if the motor and battery can pull it through the wood. The 12 inch Greenworks and Seesii are better matched to their packs. Bar length sets the largest log; power sets how quickly it cuts. A common mistake is buying the longest bar for occasional pruning, then fighting its weight on a ladder. Pick the shortest bar that cuts the biggest limb you expect.

The Snoonwee runs two 4.0Ah packs in series for 42V, and the ReliaRoads runs two 20V packs together. Series layouts raise torque. A single 20V pack in the FXAFXA cannot match that. Check whether a kit ships with one pack or two, because a second pack doubles your working time while the first charges.
The ReliaRoads claims 54 ft/s, the FXAFXA about 33 ft/s, and mini saws around 28. A faster chain cuts cleaner. Treat all of these as manufacturer claims.
Tool-free tensioning lets you tighten a stretched chain in the field. Auto oiling protects the chain. Both reduce chores, and the Greenworks, Seesii and ReliaRoads include them.
The Greenworks has a dual start with lock and trigger and a low-recoil chain. The FXAFXA has a hand guard. Always use eye protection, gloves and a firm stance.

A named brand like Greenworks means packs and chains are easy to find. Unbranded saws leave you with the seller. Check pack availability before buying. Third-party tools that run on DeWalt packs save money if you own the batteries, but the tool warranty is separate from DeWalt's.

cards.label: Branded
cards.text: The Greenworks 40V gives easy replacement packs and a safer start system. It has smaller battery capacity for the money.

cards.label: Unbranded
cards.text: The Snoonwee, Seesii, FXAFXA and ReliaRoads offer more bar and battery per dollar. Support rests on the seller.

howToChoose.note: Pick branded for long-term support; pick unbranded for more hardware at the same cap.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A longer bar, a series battery layout and a spare chain. Expect to cut small rounds, not hardwood by the cord.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Snoonwee 42V is the best match. The 12 inch saws fit smaller limbs.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You cut firewood weekly, fell trees or want long-term support. A premium platform saw is the better tool.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You clear storm debris once or twice a year. The FXAFXA or Greenworks is enough.

maintenance.why: A dry chain overheats and stretches. Use bar oil.
New chains stretch early. Tool-free knobs make this quick.
A dull chain bogs the motor and drains the pack. A sharp chain pulls itself into the wood, while a dull one needs force that increases kickback risk.
Sawdust blocks the oil path and wears the sprocket.
Cells age faster when full or empty. Keep them cool.

faq.q: Can a cordless saw replace a gas saw?
faq.a: For homeowner work, yes. For daily heavy cutting, no. Battery saws in this tier suit limbing and light firewood.

It applies to the listing price on the day this guide was updated, and prices move. The ReliaRoads lists no batteries, so check what you get. Add the cost of bar oil, a spare chain and safety gear to your budget.
For limbing and small logs, yes. For bigger trunks, choose a 16 or 18 inch bar.
Two packs wired together to add voltage. It raises torque, as in the Snoonwee. It needs a matched pair of packs and a charger that can refill both, so check that the kit includes the charger.
They are ratings, not measured outputs. Judge by bar length, battery layout and chain speed.

faq.q: How do I reduce kickback risk?
faq.a: Use a low-recoil chain, keep a firm two-hand grip and avoid cutting with the bar tip. Never cut above shoulder height, and keep the saw below the waist when carrying it.
